ontology.A_scenario: Unchanged 3x3 simultaneous assignment, 300 periods, 20 paired evaluation seeds; exact exogenous competence, demand and potential reward noise from original D0/D1/D2 scenario.
ontology.B_mechanism: Competence is exogenous, not MIS-v2 or Nembhard learning. Bernoulli outcomes are generated as before. LinUCB policy learning observes only selected-pair rewards.
ontology.C_organization: Trained fixed map; LinUCB+matching with/without competence context; LinUCB+greedy with competence context; existing P0 reactive matching; evaluator-only dynamic oracle.
ontology.policy_learning_vs_agent_learning: LinUCB updates policy parameters from selected feedback; no agent competence changes are caused by decisions.

configuration.demand: Exactly the existing StationaryTaskDemand/C5 path, all three tasks every period.
configuration.competence: Exact existing competence_path; policy independent and bounded; no changes to D0/D1/D2 parameters.
configuration.reward: Same potential Bernoulli outcome for every agent-task-period, generated by existing _potential_uniforms. Policies observe feedback only for selected edges.
configuration.context_full: Existing x_ikt=(observed current competence C_ikt,), one scalar; original per-pair disjoint LinUCB, alpha=alpha_from_delta(0.05)=2.3581015157406195, unchanged equations.
configuration.context_ablation: Task identity one-hot (three features), no competence or regime feature. Same disjoint LinUCB update and alpha; per-pair identity is also represented by separate models. No latent regime labels are supplied.
configuration.p0: Existing P0ProductionOnlyNK applied to the six feasible perfect-matching allocations using only observed C and public unit requirements. It ranks additive outputs via the existing success/deficit/margin/effort tuple; it receives no reward matrix, future path or oracle action. In this public scenario E[R_ikt]=C_ikt, so its current score is model-implied, not privileged evaluator input.
configuration.resources: All policies produce exactly one unit assignment per agent and task each period: 3 units/period, 900 per episode.
configuration.fixed_opt: Same 3! fixed-map enumeration trained separately for each condition on existing 20 training seeds, evaluated on the same 20 held-out seeds as all other policies.
configuration.oracle: True current expected reward matrix used only by evaluator for comparator, regret, assignment agreement and preflight; never passed into executable policies.
configuration.random_streams: Competence seed = evaluation_seed XOR 0xC05E7E; potential Bernoulli uniforms = evaluation_seed XOR 0xA11CE; C5 demand is generated by the existing seed-based trajectory generator. These are identical to the original sensitivity runner.

limitations: Synthetic reward has the public identity E[R]=competence, so P0 can exploit the declared model exactly; this is not a test of estimation under model misspecification.

P0 versus LinUCB changes both decision rule and learning; the clean statistical-learning contrast is LinUCB full versus LinUCB without competence context, while P0 versus full-context LinUCB compares known model-responsive P0 against estimation/exploration.
The competence-context ablation removes a direct state feature but keeps task identity; given separate pair models and static task identities, task identity carries little within-pair variation.
D1 and D2 change amplitude and persistence jointly, so their contributions are not identified separately.
Twenty paired seeds are exploratory/descriptive, not confirmatory. Paired t intervals are descriptive only.
This experiment concerns exogenous competence and policy learning, not endogenous MIS-v2 learning or transfer.
